authors.description: Author list as given on the paper.
authors.title: Authors

benchmark_names.description: Named benchmark(s), dataset(s), corpus(es), or exam(s) that the LLM was EVALUATED ON in arms that pass the MH relevance gate. EVALUATION-ONLY RULE: include ONLY datasets/corpora/exams used as evaluation material — the inputs the LLM was scored on. Do NOT include training corpora, fine-tuning datasets, RLHF preference datasets, or datasets mentioned only in the model's provenance. E.g. a paper that fine-tunes on ESConv and evaluates on PsyQA lists ['PsyQA'], not ['ESConv', 'PsyQA']. NAME AS THE PAPER NAMES IT: transcribe the name exactly as it appears in this paper's methods section. Do NOT supply familiar canonical names for corpora the paper describes without naming. If the paper says 'we sampled 100 posts from a Reddit mental-health forum' without naming the corpus, leave that unnamed (do not tag as 'Reddit MH corpus' or similar). If the paper names it 'MHRedditSet-v2', use exactly that. WORK FROM THE ARM LIST, NOT THE DATASET SECTION: enumerate the evaluation arms first (task × input × reference standard × scoring), then list the named benchmark used in each in-scope arm. Do not scrape the dataset section for names — some named datasets there may belong only to training or excluded arms. Named exams count: USMLE, PRITE, MRCPsych, Portuguese National Residency Access Examination (PNA), Chinese Medical Licensing Examination count even when the paper does not say 'benchmark.' SCOPE RESTRICTION: include ONLY benchmarks used in arms that pass the MH relevance gate. Non-MH benchmarks from arms excluded at the gate do NOT appear here. A paper evaluating on MMLU + MedQA + PsyQA where only PsyQA is MH-relevant lists only ['PsyQA']. Per-benchmark rule: if the same benchmark appears in BOTH an included and an excluded arm, it stays. LIST EACH BENCHMARK ONCE per paper regardless of how many in-scope arms use it. WORKED EXAMPLE: a paper with 8 named benchmarks used across 13 arms where 3 arms are MH-relevant and use 2 of the 8 benchmarks — list those 2 benchmarks, once each. DO NOT include validated clinical or research instruments used as REFERENCE STANDARDS (C-SSRS, PHQ-9, PHQ-8, GAD-7, CAPS-5, HAM-D, HAMD-17, MADRS, YMRS, PANSS, WAI, CTRS, MITI, PANAS, etc.). Those go in reference_standard_instruments, not here. Include a named instrument here ONLY when the scale items are the INPUT to the LLM. Rule of thumb: does the LLM SEE the scale items? If yes → benchmark_names candidate; if no (scale is only how outputs are graded) → reference_standard_instruments. Do NOT include the name of the model, framework, or system being EVALUATED — that goes in systems_tested / models_tested. E.g. 'SAGE' is a framework being evaluated, not a benchmark. Same for chatbot names (Sarah, BeFreeGPT, etc.). BUT: 'FRAMEWORK' IS NOT A CARVE-OUT (clarified 2026-08-29.10). This exclusion is about the OBJECT OF EVALUATION, not the word the paper uses. Ask which side of the test the named thing sits on. If it is a system being SCORED, exclude it. If it is the apparatus DOING the scoring and it owns a named, fixed input set, it is a benchmark and belongs here — even when the paper calls it a framework, a harness, a pipeline, or an environment, and even when it holds no static transcripts. WORKED EXAMPLE: MindEval calls itself 'a framework' in its abstract and was wrongly left null. It names itself in its title, lists 'MindEval (ours)' in a table of benchmarks, and owns a fixed set of 50 patient profiles against which every system under test is run. benchmark_names = ['MindEval']. A benchmark whose fixed component is the stimulus generator rather than the stimuli is still a benchmark. COROLLARY: if the paper introduces a named evaluation artefact at all — which type_of_study = 'Benchmark development' asserts — this field cannot be null. Leave null if the input source is not named — do NOT invent a name.CONVENTION: use null (not an empty list) when this field does not apply to the paper. An empty list is never a valid value for this field.
benchmark_names.title: Benchmark Names

type_of_study.description: Benchmark development: paper BUILDS an evaluation apparatus of its own. Judge by what was BUILT, not by whether the artifact is named, released, or fully specified. Tag Benchmark development when ANY of these apply: (a) constructs or curates an ITEM SET with stated selection or generation criteria; (b) designs an ORIGINAL GRADING INSTRUMENT — a new rubric, autograder, or LLM-judge system, including one validated against human raters as part of the paper; (c) designs an ORIGINAL SCORING PROTOCOL or METRIC VARIANT — a new adherence checklist, severity coding scheme, or adapted composite metric. Naming, release, and full specification are NOT required. Evaluation study: paper evaluates existing models on existing benchmarks / instruments / protocols without building any of the three above. Prompt engineering alone = Evaluation study. Model development: fine-tuning, RLHF, or architectural modification. Prompt-only guardrail / classifier systems built on an existing generative LLM are NOT Model development. PRIORITY RULE — when multiple categories apply, prefer: Benchmark development > Model development > Evaluation study. A paper that both develops a benchmark AND evaluates existing models on it (SHIELD-style: new benchmark + baseline rates on 5 LLMs) → Benchmark development. A paper that fine-tunes a model AND evaluates it → Model development. Only papers with no new benchmark and no model changes are Evaluation study. WORKED EXAMPLE: a paper writes 30 clinical consultation templates against stated inclusion criteria, has GPT-4 and Claude complete each one, and scores completions with a new 5-point adherence rubric. Even without a benchmark name → Benchmark development.
type_of_study.title: Type Of Study

mh_scope.description: Whether mental health is the SOLE focus of the paper or one of several domains covered. Populated after applying the relevance gate. MH only: every arm is MH-relevant; no non-MH content was excluded at the gate. Typical of dedicated MH benchmark papers, MH-specific chatbot evaluations. Mixed — MH is a substantial domain: the paper covers multiple domains (general medicine including MH, multi-specialty clinical evaluations, broad LLM benchmarks with MH as one section) AND MH is a substantial portion — a distinct section, a named domain, ~20-25%+ of results. Mixed — MH is a minor domain: paper primarily about a non-MH topic (general medical exam, multi-domain benchmark) with MH as a small subset. Included only when results are disaggregated for the MH subset.
enum: Mixed — MH is a substantial domain
Mixed — MH is a minor domain
mh_scope.title: Mh Scope

journal_source.description: Publication venue. For preprints, use the server name: 'arXiv', 'medRxiv', 'bioRxiv', 'PsyArXiv'. For peer-reviewed articles, the journal name. For conference papers, the conference name (e.g., 'NeurIPS 2024', 'EMNLP 2023'). Null if unclear.
journal_source.title: Journal Source

journal_source_type.description: Category of publication venue. IMPORTANT: many arXiv / preprint uploads are actually conference papers. Before defaulting to Preprint, check for conference signals — author-block cites the conference ('To appear at NeurIPS 2024', 'Accepted at EMNLP 2023'), camera-ready formatting, DOI pointing to a conference, or paper explicitly names a conference. If ANY conference signal is present → Conference proceeding, not Preprint. Preprint is ONLY for uploads with no evidence of formal venue publication. Preprint: arXiv, medRxiv, bioRxiv, PsyArXiv, or other preprint server, with NO conference or journal affiliation visible. Conference proceeding: NeurIPS, EMNLP, ACL, CHI, AMIA, etc. — includes conference papers hosted on preprint servers if conference affiliation is stated. Peer reviewed: journal article that went through peer review. Other: thesis, technical report, book chapter, etc. — include a brief inline specifier when possible.
journal_source_type.title: Journal Source Type

system_tasks.description: System tasks performed by the SYSTEM UNDER EVALUATION — the model(s) whose performance the paper measures and reports as results. IMPORTANT: distinguish evaluated systems from models used in the evaluation methodology (LLM-as-judge, annotators, raters, data generators, score assigners). System tasks describe ONLY what the evaluated system does. Never include tasks performed by judge/annotator models — those methodology roles do not contribute task labels to the evaluated system's record. TAG THE FEWEST TASKS across the paper (deduplicated) that fully describe what the evaluated systems are doing. Do not add tags for peripheral behaviors. MCQ vs CLASSIFICATION — THE POSED-QUESTION TEST (added 2026-08-29.10). Multiple-choice answering is ALWAYS 'Question-answering', never 'Classification / score prediction', regardless of subject matter. If the item presents the model with a QUESTION plus a fixed set of candidate answers, it is Question-answering. If the model is handed MATERIAL and asked to assign a label or score from a schema it was told about but that is not offered as options on the item, it is Classification / score prediction. Format, not topic: a diagnostic MCQ over a clinical vignette is still Question-answering, because the model picks among presented options. WORKED PAIR: MAGneT scores CounselingBench MCQs -> Question-answering (correct). MentalBench asks 'What is the most likely diagnosis? A/B/C/D' over a vignette -> Question-answering (was coded Classification; this is the corrected value). CONTRAST, both stay Classification: WundtGPT assigns one of nine emotion labels to an utterance with no options presented; Kumar assigns MITI Likert scores to a summary. Those are the LLM-as-annotator family, which the constructs vocabulary already treats separately (Psychotherapy process annotation, Stigma and harmful-content detection). RATIONALE: MCQ answering is common in this corpus, so splitting it across two codes empties both columns; reserving Classification for annotation-of-material makes the field separate two genuinely different setups. The MCQ format itself is already carried by input_formats. Classification / score prediction: covers both DISCRETE label/tier assignment scored by exact-match / F1 (severity tier, diagnosis, risk category) AND CONTINUOUS numeric prediction scored by RMSE / MAE / CCC / correlation (PHQ-8 continuous 0-24, BFI-10 Likert items, well-being scale totals). Both go here — record the discrete-vs-continuous distinction and specific scoring metric in scoring_procedures. If a paper does both on the same input, list Classification / score prediction once. EXCLUSION: Classification / score prediction does NOT cover judgment-about-another-party's-performance. When the evaluated system is asked to grade, rate, judge, or score another system's or a human's output, that is Evaluation/judging. Classification is about assigning a label to an input; Evaluation/judging is about assessing a performance. Evaluation/judging: the evaluated system is being scored on how well it grades, rates, or assesses another party's outputs (LLM-as-judge validation studies, autograder evaluations). Do NOT tag when a judge is used only as evaluation methodology to score another system's outputs. PREEMPTION IS PER-SYSTEM, NOT PER-STUDY: when Evaluation/judging applies to a system, do not also tag Classification / score prediction or Text/response generation FOR THAT SAME SYSTEM'S ROLE — a judge emitting an integer rubric rating is Evaluation/judging alone. But this field aggregates across the paper's arms, so a STUDY may carry Evaluation/judging ALONGSIDE other tasks performed by DIFFERENT systems: a paper that scores counsellor LLMs on generated dialogue AND validates its own LLM judge against human ratings has BOTH Text/response generation AND Evaluation/judging. Record every task any evaluated system performs. WHEN DOES A JUDGE COUNT AT ALL: only when the judge is ITSELF EVALUATED — the paper reports its agreement with human raters, its correlation with expert scores, or its accuracy against a labelled standard. An LLM judge used purely as apparatus, whose own quality is never scored, is methodology: do NOT record Evaluation/judging and do NOT list 'LLM as judge/evaluator' in systems_tested. Other includes agentic task execution / tool use (multi-step planning workflows). Use Other with a brief 1-2 sentence description in abstraction_notes explaining the task and why no other category fits — do not use Other as a default. OUT OF SCOPE — do NOT record: qualitative coding / thematic analysis (inductive code development, excerpt extraction, theme synthesis); text / information extraction tasks (pulling entities, spans, structured fields from text). These are qualitative research or NLP methodology outside our review's clinical-capability scope. If a paper's only evaluation is qualitative coding or text extraction, exclude the paper. Select all that apply across the paper, deduplicated.
system_tasks.title: System Tasks

mental_health_domains.description: Mental health domain(s) the LLM is EVALUATED on, deduplicated. The vocabulary is enforced: any value outside it, other than an inline 'Other (specifier)', is rejected. Include a domain ONLY if the paper reports quantitative results for the LLM's performance in that domain — never from the Introduction, Related Work, Discussion, or proposed future applications. GENERAL-CODES RULE: 'General mental health' and 'General psychology' are for use ONLY when no specific condition or context is identifiable, and NEVER alongside a specific domain code. Category boundaries, multi-domain-instrument handling, and the construct-versus-domain distinctions (Misinformation vs Guideline adherence; Bias vs Fairness / equity; Cognitive distortion vs Diagnostic accuracy; Delusional disorder vs LLM delusion confirmation) are in the MENTAL HEALTH DOMAINS section of the extraction guide.
mental_health_domains.title: Mental Health Domains

evaluation_constructs_described.description: Evaluation constructs AS DESCRIBED BY THE AUTHORS in their own words — dimensions or criteria they name in the paper. Short phrases, not overly detailed. Paired with evaluation_constructs_categories (the controlled vocabulary mapping) to let reviewers audit categorization decisions. E.g. ['Guidance', 'Informativeness', 'Interpretation', 'Empathy', 'Helpfulness', 'Safety']; ['affective attitude', 'burden', 'ethicality', 'coherence (Sekhon TFA)', 'opportunity cost', 'perceived effectiveness', 'hallucination extent']. Preserve the paper's own terminology — do not translate to controlled vocabulary here. Deduplicate across arms.
evaluation_constructs_described.title: Evaluation Constructs Described

evaluation_constructs_categories.description: Evaluation construct(s) the paper REPORTS QUANTITATIVE RESULTS FOR, mapped to the controlled vocabulary. The vocabulary is enforced: any value outside it, other than an inline 'Other (specifier)', is rejected. FULL DEFINITIONS, the Object Test, the Reference-Standard Test, the five procedural rules, and the referral routing rule are in the EVALUATION CONSTRUCTS section of the extraction guide. Apply them there; this description states only the invariants. (1) EVIDENCE. Every construct must correspond to a reported quantitative result. Terminology in the title, abstract, taxonomy, Related Work, or Discussion is not evidence of measurement. (2) TEST PRECEDENCE. Apply the OBJECT TEST first — is the construct scored on the INPUT the model was given, or the OUTPUT it produced? Only when both candidates score the same object does the REFERENCE-STANDARD TEST decide. Where the two tests point different ways, the OBJECT TEST WINS. Worked case: MITI's Empathy global rating scores the output (Object Test → Empathy) but comes from a normative manual (Reference-Standard Test → Therapeutic technique fidelity). Object Test wins only if the paper reports that subscale SEPARATELY; if it is folded into an overall MITI fidelity score, the scored object is the session, not the response, and the answer is Therapeutic technique fidelity. (3) ONE PARADIGM, ONE ENTRY. If two constructs would draw on the same reported result, at most one is correct. (4) ONE INSTRUMENT, ONE CONSTRUCT. Each validated instrument is one paradigm mapped to a single construct — its closest controlled term, or 'Other (instrument name)'. Do NOT split an instrument's subscales into separate constructs, and do NOT collapse multiple distinct instruments into one best-fit entry. A paper using CTRS, WAI, and PANAS yields THREE constructs, one per instrument — not eleven subscale entries and not one list. (5) BARE AUTOMATED METRICS. When the only construct-relevant evaluation is one or more bare automated metrics against gold responses (BERTScore, perplexity, ROUGE) with no qualitative dimensions, map to a SINGLE holistic construct, normally Response quality — not several stretched near-mappings. The metrics belong in scoring_procedures. (6) DIRECT NAME MATCHES TAKE PRECEDENCE. When a paper's own dimension name appears verbatim in the vocabulary and collides with a default mapping — the paper reports both 'Guidance' and 'Helpfulness' as separate dimensions, and Guidance normally maps to Helpfulness — map the direct match first, then find an alternative for the other. Do not force both into one term. (7) RESPONSE QUALITY IS RESIDUAL. Use it for a holistic rating the paper does NOT break into named dimensions. An ARITHMETIC MEAN OR COMPOSITE OF DIMENSIONS ALREADY MAPPED IS NOT A DISTINCT RESULT — do not add Response quality for it. Add it alongside specific constructs only when an overall score is separately elicited from raters or otherwise measured independently of the named dimensions. (8) EXCLUSIONS. Never record statistical or calibration metrics (F1, AUROC, ECE, Brier, coverage), robustness, efficiency, reproducibility, or judge-reliability metrics. Constructs must not duplicate system_tasks. Out-of-scope author dimensions (response coherence, relevance, semantic similarity, usability, engagement, response speed, user-reported trust / credibility / satisfaction / acceptance) go in evaluation_constructs_described and are NOT mapped here — a _described list longer than this one is expected and is not an error.
evaluation_constructs_categories.title: Evaluation Constructs Categories

primary_construct.description: THE SINGLE construct this paper is primarily about — the one a reader scanning the corpus would say the paper measures. Analysis runs on this column; evaluation_constructs_categories keeps the full detail. MUST be one of the values in evaluation_constructs_categories. If that list has one entry, this is that entry. SELECTION ORDER, applied in sequence until one rule decides: (1) HEADLINE RESULT. The construct behind the finding the abstract leads with, or the result reported first in the results section. THE HEADLINE IS THE NUMBER REPORTED, NOT THE FRAMING THAT MOTIVATES IT (added 2026-08-29.10). Titles, motivations and contribution claims are not results. If the reported headline is a COMPOSITE of several dimensions, the primary is what that composite measures, and a construct carried by only one sub-dimension can never be primary. WORKED EXAMPLE: Hasan is titled and motivated around culturally-grounded knowledge, but cultural appropriateness is one parenthetical qualifier inside one of five human dimensions, and the headline number is the five-dimension mean improving under KG grounding. Cultural sensitivity belongs in the categories list; it is NOT the primary. (2) ANCHORING INSTRUMENT. If one validated instrument anchors the evaluation, take the construct that instrument maps to — CTRS or MITI anchoring a counselling evaluation gives Therapeutic technique fidelity even when secondary dimensions map elsewhere. (3) WEIGHT OF EVIDENCE. The construct with the most separately reported quantitative results behind it. (4) SPECIFICITY. Never choose 'Response quality' or an 'Other (specifier)' entry when a specific named construct is available; residual and catch-all terms lose to named ones. If two constructs remain genuinely tied after all four rules, pick either, flag primary_construct in abstraction_flags, and name the alternative in abstraction_notes.
primary_construct.title: Primary Construct

systems_tested.description: All system-tested types evaluated across the paper, deduplicated.
systems_tested.title: Systems Tested

evaluated_output_types.description: All evaluated-output types across the paper's arms, deduplicated. What the evaluated system OUTPUTS: Generated text (open-ended text judged on content/quality/safety), Label or class (discrete categorical output scored by exact match / F1 / accuracy), Score or rating (numeric or ordinal score emitted by the model, scored by RMSE / MAE / correlation), Mixed (arm combines two or more output types). Different from system_tasks — a QA task can be Generated text (free-text answers) or Label or class (MCQ options) with different scoring machinery.
evaluated_output_types.title: Evaluated Output Types

input_formats.description: All input formats used across the paper, deduplicated. Classify by NATIVE form, not by prompt serialization. Use 'Other (specify)' rather than the nearest-sounding category.
input_formats.title: Input Formats

input_provenance_types.description: WHO ASSEMBLED the input item set, deduplicated across the paper. This is one of two orthogonal questions about the inputs; the other is input_reality, which asks what the material IS. Answer them independently — all four combinations occur, and neither answer constrains the other. Third-party: items assembled by other researchers — established benchmarks, published datasets, prior-work corpora (DAIC-WOZ, ESConv, PsyQA, CounselChat, USMLE, PRITE, MRCPsych, MedQA, Dreaddit, EmpatheticDialogues, CLPsych). A subset of a third-party benchmark is still Third-party, and so is a vignette reproduced from an earlier paper. Author-created: items assembled by the AUTHORS of this paper — vignettes they wrote, IRB data they collected, inputs they generated with an LLM, data they scraped and curated, questions they wrote ad hoc. Release status does not change this: an author-created dataset the authors release is still Author-created. Mixed: use ONLY for a single arm drawing from both sources inseparably. A paper with one Third-party arm and one Author-created arm lists BOTH values, not Mixed. Item release is a separate question again, captured in input_availabilities.
input_provenance_types.title: Input Provenance Types

input_availabilities.description: Whether another investigator could obtain or reconstruct the evaluation ITEMS themselves, deduplicated across arms. Judge item access only. Publicly released: items downloadable without gate or request. Available on request: items obtainable via author request, DUA, IRB registration. Fully specified in paper: every item reproduced in text, tables, figures, or appendix. Method reproducible, items unavailable: procedure released but items themselves (e.g. PHI clinical records, proprietary transcripts) cannot be obtained. Partially specified: illustrative items shown but full set not recoverable. Not available: neither items nor reconstructible procedure reported. DEFAULT AND EVIDENCE RULE (added 2026-08-29.11). 'Not available' is the DEFAULT. Silence is not availability: if the paper contains no repository link, no data-availability statement, and no sentence offering the items, the answer is 'Not available' and no inference is permitted from the fact that the authors seem cooperative, the data seem shareable, or similar work is usually released. ANY value other than 'Not available' requires POSITIVE EVIDENCE quoted or cited in abstraction_notes — a URL, a named repository, a data-availability section, or the sentence offering access. In particular 'Available on request' requires the paper to actually SAY the items are available on request; it is not the polite default for unreleased data. WHY: across three identical runs this field flipped Hasan between 'Available on request' and 'Not available', and the Hasan paper says nothing whatever about availability — the non-default value was invented, not read. Replaces the older input_reproducibility field.
input_availabilities.title: Input Availabilities

input_determinism.description: WHAT GENERATES THE VARIATION in the evaluation inputs, deduplicated across the paper's INCLUDED arms. Renamed from input_standardizations 2026-08-29.11 because that name asked a DIFFERENT question (whether all systems face the same inputs). That question is NOT recorded by this tool — see the note at the end of this description. VALUES ARE NON-EXCLUSIVE — record every mechanism that applies. The former 'PRECEDENCE OVER ITERATIVE' rule, which forced a single pick, is DELETED: it was the direct cause of this field's instability, because simulation papers are genuinely several of these at once. Fixed: items are determined BEFORE the evaluation begins and do not change during it. Provenance is irrelevant (third-party, author-created and mixed sources can all be Fixed). Prompt variants over a fixed item set are still Fixed. Single-system papers can be Fixed. Stochastic: inputs are drawn or generated fresh per trial or per run — GENERATION AT CONSTRUCTION TIME IS NOT STOCHASTICITY (added 2026-08-29.18). The test is whether inputs are REGENERATED WHEN A NEW SYSTEM IS BENCHMARKED, not whether generation happened at all. A synthetic corpus that was generated once, frozen, and reused unchanged for every system is Fixed and ONLY Fixed, however it was produced. CONTRAST: MentalBench generated 24,750 cases once and froze them — every model sees the identical set — so it is Fixed alone; coding it Stochastic because the cases are LLM-generated is an error observed in testing. MindEval keeps a fixed pool of 50 patient profiles but generates a fresh set of interactions each time a system is benchmarked, so it is Fixed AND Stochastic AND Dynamic. Ask: if I benchmark a new model tomorrow, does it face the same items? Yes -> Fixed. LLM-generated scenarios, random corpus sampling without a pinned sample, ad hoc constructed prompts. Dynamic: later inputs depend on the model's OWN earlier outputs — multi-turn interactive beyond the opening, agentic loops, self-play. Live: inputs come from real users of a deployed system and drift outside the investigators' control. Mixed or unclear: the paper does not report enough to tell. Use sparingly; it is not a substitute for listing two applicable values. WORKED EXAMPLE (MindEval) — THREE values, all true: Fixed (a pinned pool of 50 patient profiles, reused for every system), Stochastic (a fresh set of interactions is generated each time a system is benchmarked), Dynamic (within an interaction, later turns condition on earlier ones). Under the old precedence rule the extractor had to choose one, and chose differently on different runs. WHAT THIS FIELD DOES AND DOES NOT SUPPORT. Fixed ALONE implies the inputs are reproducible across runs — that inference is safe. Fixed does NOT imply the compared systems were scored on the SAME items, and this tool does not record that. Systems may be scored on different subsets, on model-specific prompt variants over one item set (still coded Fixed), or in separate arms this rollup collapses; and single-system papers can be Fixed with no comparison at all. Conversely not-Fixed does not imply the systems faced different items — MindEval regenerates every interaction yet every system faces the identical pool of 50 profiles. Do not use this field to support a claim about cross-system comparability in either direction.
input_determinism.title: Input Determinism

parent_benchmarks.description: Names of pre-existing EVALUATION BENCHMARKS (item sets) that any benchmark in this paper reuses as a composite or derivation, deduplicated across the paper. Populated ONLY when a benchmark used in an in-scope arm derives from or composites items drawn from another named evaluation benchmark. Direct reuse of an existing benchmark (or a subset of one) leaves this None. RESERVED FOR EVALUATION ITEM SETS. Do NOT include: (a) validated clinical instruments (PHQ-9, GAD-7, C-SSRS, WAI, CTRS, etc.) — these are scoring instruments or reference standards, not parent benchmarks; (b) diagnostic taxonomies or classification systems (DSM-5, ICD-10, ICD-11, RDoC) — these are frameworks the benchmark is built AGAINST, not parents; (c) evaluation frameworks or theoretical models (Sekhon TFA, TAM, SUS, HBM, Bloom's taxonomy) — these are rubric frameworks, not item sources; (d) base foundation models, checkpoints, or training corpora — those belong in models_tested or in the model's provenance section, not here; (e) benchmarks cited only in Related Work or Discussion as comparisons — the parent must have actually contributed items to this paper's benchmark; (f) benchmarks the paper's benchmark is merely INSPIRED BY or CONCEPTUALLY similar to — the parent must have contributed actual items. MULTI-LEVEL CHAINS: if benchmark A derives from B which derives from C, list only IMMEDIATE parent B here. Note the deeper chain in abstraction_notes. DERIVED-FROM vs USED-DIRECTLY: language matters. 'Composed of items sampled from X' or 'Built by adapting items from X' → X is a parent. 'Uses X' or 'Evaluated on X' with no modification → X IS the input, not a parent (goes in benchmark_names, not parent_benchmarks). Hedged language like 'inspired by' or 'similar to' → NOT a parent. Use canonical names to enable cross-study aggregation (SafetyBench, TrustGPT, MedSafetyBench, DAIC-WOZ, ESConv, PsyQA, CounselChat, USMLE question banks, etc.). SEEDED GENERATION IS DERIVATION (added 2026-08-29.10). When this paper's items are GENERATED from seeds, profiles, cases or prompts taken from another named benchmark, that benchmark is a parent, even though every resulting item is new text. The test is item-level traceability: can each new item be traced back to a specific item in the source set? WORKED EXAMPLE: MAGneT generates synthetic counselling sessions from 150 client intake profiles taken from CACTUS, each session anchored to one profile — CACTUS is a parent AND, being an evaluation set the study involves, also belongs in benchmark_names. CONTRASTING NON-EXAMPLES: MindEval's attribute pool is 'inspired by' Patient-psi with no items carried over (parent = None, per the hedged-language rule above); MentalBench builds MentalKG from DSM-5 text, which is a taxonomy and is excluded by (b) above (parent = None). Example: XTRUST-MH is a composite of SafetyBench + TrustGPT + MedSafetyBench → parent_benchmarks = ['SafetyBench', 'TrustGPT', 'MedSafetyBench']; input_provenance_types still includes 'Author-created' because the composite is new.CONVENTION: use null (not an empty list) when this field does not apply to the paper. An empty list is never a valid value for this field.
parent_benchmarks.title: Parent Benchmarks

populations.description: All populations the inputs represent across the paper, deduplicated. High-level, population-focused. E.g. 'adults with depression', 'psychiatric outpatients', 'mental health clinicians', 'general public'. Do not indicate real vs. synthetic. Use 'Not applicable' ONLY when the input has no represented population — pure knowledge or factual questions ('Which SSRI has the shortest half-life?', 'Define bipolar disorder'), definitions, terminology quizzes, or generic prompts where the LLM is answering about FACTS rather than about a person or population. Format is not the deciding factor — what matters is what the LLM is being asked to reason about. If the input consists of case vignettes, patient scenarios, symptom presentations, or clinical descriptions — EVEN when drawn from exam banks, textbooks, or casebooks — the population is who those cases represent (e.g., 'adult psychiatric patients as depicted in authoritative textbooks and casebooks', 'adolescents with anxiety presenting to primary care').
populations.title: Populations

output_audiences.description: All target audiences for the LLM's outputs across the paper, deduplicated. Who the LLM's response is INTENDED FOR — distinct from populations (who inputs represent). Patient / Consumer: lay user, patient, help-seeker, general consumer (chatbot user, help-seeking letter response, self-help content). Provider: healthcare provider, clinician, physician, therapist, licensed practitioner, OR trainee in a provider-oriented role (medical student, resident, counselor-in-training). Covers clinical decision support, differential diagnosis, treatment recommendation, chart review, exam-answering for provider trainees, and training-scenario content. Researcher: LLM output serves research (data annotation, coding, classification, benchmark scoring). Mixed: use as a value only if a single arm targets multiple audiences. Not applicable: LLM capability testing without a specific intended audience (pure knowledge testing, exam-answering scored on correctness). Deduplicate across arms — a paper with provider-facing and patient-facing arms lists both.
output_audiences.title: Output Audiences

input_reality.description: What the input material IS, deduplicated across the paper. This field asks about theNATURE OF THE DATA and is deliberately orthogonal to input_provenance_types, which asksWHO ASSEMBLED IT. The two answers are independent: authors can assemble real data(Author-created + Real), and a third-party benchmark can consist of LLM-generatedvignettes (Third-party + Synthetic — LLM-generated). Never reason about authorship here.Real: material that arose from actual human activity outside the study — clinicalrecords, therapy or hotline transcripts, social-media posts, forum threads, examquestion banks, published corpora of naturally occurring text. Synthetic — human-written: material a person wrote for research or assessment purposes rather than in thecourse of real life — clinician-authored vignettes, researcher-written prompts,constructed case scenarios, hand-built question sets. This applies whether the personwho wrote it was an author of this paper or of a prior one; a vignette taken from anearlier publication and reproduced here is Synthetic — human-written, withinput_provenance_types = Third-party. Synthetic — LLM-generated: material produced by alanguage model or simulator — LLM-generated patient scenarios, simulator dialogue turns,model-authored vignettes. Mixed: a single arm combines two of the above and they cannotbe cleanly separated. Use separate list entries, not Mixed, when different arms havedifferent answers. Not reported: the paper does not say.
input_reality.title: Input Reality

input_languages.description: Language(s) of input data across the paper, deduplicated. Canonical English names: English, Mandarin (not Chinese), Standard Arabic if specified (otherwise Arabic), Spanish, French, German, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, etc. A multilingual benchmark lists all languages. Use ['Not reported'] if language is not specified. Do not infer language from author affiliation.
input_languages.title: Input Languages

conversation_types.description: How stimulus is structured and how model outputs relate to prior outputs, rolled up across the paper. Single-shot: the model produces ONE scored output per item AND its own prior outputs never appear in its input. Covers non-dialogue stimuli (MCQ, vignette, post, document, standalone question) AND dialogue stimuli where the model answers once (dialogue classification / scoring, next-response generation on gold history). Whether the stimulus is a dialogue does NOT matter here — that is carried by input_formats and system_tasks. Multi-turn interactive: model produces outputs at multiple points in an evolving exchange; later turns are conditioned on the model's own earlier outputs (with real users, scripted interlocutors, or LLM seeker-simulators; LLM-vs-LLM self-play qualifies). Mixed: paper includes arms of more than one type. Not applicable: LLM does not produce outputs in the paper (e.g. benchmark-only papers with no reported model results). Distinguishing test between Single-shot and Multi-turn interactive: does the model's own earlier output feed back into its later input? If yes → Multi-turn interactive; if no → Single-shot.
conversation_types.title: Conversation Types

dataset_purpose.description: What the paper's evaluation data is USED FOR, rolled up across the study. Distinct from type_of_study, which records what the paper contributes; this field records what the data does. A Model development paper can fine-tune on one corpus and evaluate on a third-party benchmark, and an Evaluation study can build data it only ever scores against. 'Evaluation only': the data exists to score systems and is never used to update model weights. 'Training or tuning only': the data is used to fine-tune, distil, RLHF, or continue-pretrain a model, and no arm scores systems on it. TRAINING IS BROADER THAN FINE-TUNING — distillation, preference tuning and continued pretraining all count. 'Both — held-out split reported': some data trains and some evaluates, AND the paper describes a held-out split, test set, or other separation. 'Both — split not reported': some data trains and some evaluates, and the paper does not describe a separation. 'Not applicable': no evaluation data in the paper (e.g. position or survey papers). FEW-SHOT EXEMPLARS ARE NOT TRAINING. Items placed in a prompt as examples are prompt construction, not weight updates. MindEval draws 5 annotated interactions as judge exemplars and is 'Evaluation only'. In-context learning, retrieval augmentation and RAG corpora are likewise NOT training. DEFAULT AND EVIDENCE RULE. Between the two 'Both' values the default is 'split not reported'. Choosing 'held-out split reported' requires POSITIVE EVIDENCE quoted or cited in abstraction_notes — the sentence naming the split, the test set, or the separation. Do NOT infer a split from the fact that splitting is normal practice, that the authors are careful, or that results look clean. This value is a claim about what the paper REPORTS, not about what the authors did; 'split not reported' is a reporting-quality observation, not an accusation of leakage. DERIVATION REQUIRED FOR EITHER 'Both' VALUE: name in abstraction_notes which dataset served which purpose. MAGneT is the pattern — its own generated sessions train Llama-3-8B, CounselingBench evaluates it.
dataset_purpose.title: Dataset Purpose

reference_standard_type.description: Type(s) of reference standard used across the paper. A paper may have DIFFERENT types across arms — list all that apply, deduplicated. Pick per arm by applying this test IN ORDER — stop at the first match: AN LLM APPLYING A RUBRIC IS NEVER THE REFERENCE STANDARD (added 2026-08-29.15). Run the test below per ARM. If an arm is scored by an LLM judge and no human or ground-truth comparator exists FOR THAT ARM, it falls through to (4) and the arm is 'None — rubric-only scoring'. The judge is the scoring mechanism and belongs in scoring_procedures; it is not a comparator. READ THE VALUE CORRECTLY: 'None' scopes the COMPARATOR only. It does not mean nothing was measured — a study with neither a comparator nor a well-defined rubric would not have passed screening. The value asserts two things at once: no human or ground-truth comparator, AND a defined rubric was applied. IF THE JUDGE WAS VALIDATED AGAINST HUMANS, RECORD BOTH ARMS. The validation arm takes its own type from the test below; the benchmarking arm the judge actually scored is still 'None — rubric-only scoring'. MindEval is the pattern: 4 psychologists rate 20 interactions in the meta-evaluation (Expert/clinician ratings) while Claude-4.5-Sonnet alone scores the 600 interactions behind every headline number (None — rubric-only scoring). Recording only the first makes it read as though experts backed results they never saw. CACTUS is the same shape. (1) Is the output matched against a defined correct answer, target, or validated instrument-as-target? -> 'Ground-truth reference'. Any rubric here is only the scoring mechanism (goes in scoring_procedures). (2) If no correct answer: are QUALIFIED EXPERTS (clinicians, licensed professionals, domain experts) applying a validated framework or calibrated judgment as the comparator? -> 'Expert/clinician ratings'. AN LLM APPLYING A RUBRIC IS NEVER THE REFERENCE STANDARD (added 2026-08-29.15). A judge model is not an expert, not a trained annotator, and not a correct answer, so an LLM-scored arm falls through every step to 'None — rubric-only scoring'. Apply the test PER ARM and list every arm's result: a paper whose headline results are LLM-judged but which separately has humans rate a subset carries BOTH 'None — rubric-only scoring' and 'Expert/clinician ratings'. MindEval is exactly this: 4 psychologists rate 20 interactions in its meta-evaluation, while all 12 models in the main results are scored by Claude-4.5-Sonnet alone. Recording only the expert arm reads as though experts backed the headline numbers. READ THE VALUE NAME CAREFULLY. 'None — rubric-only scoring' does NOT mean the LLM is the standard, and does NOT mean no scoring happened. It records two things at once: (a) NO human or ground-truth comparator adjudicated these particular scores, and (b) a well-defined rubric WAS applied. Both halves matter — (b) is what keeps such a study inside the review's inclusion criteria, which require either a reference standard or a well-defined rubric. An arm with neither is not includable. MIXED RATER POOLS TAKE BOTH TYPES (added 2026-08-29.19). If one arm's raters include BOTH qualified experts and trained non-experts — '3 PhD-student annotators and 1 domain expert', 'graduate students supervised by a psychiatrist' — record Expert/clinician ratings AND Trained annotator ratings. Do not pick the more senior label; both rater types are present and both are informative. This was the single unstable reference_standard_type cell across 20 papers, and the run that listed both was the most accurate. (3) If not experts: are TRAINED NON-EXPERT annotators (research assistants, undergraduates, crowdworkers under expert-designed guidelines, coders not described as clinicians) applying a defined rubric? -> 'Trained annotator ratings'. Common for social media benchmarks, crowd-labeled data, NLP corpora. (4) If none of the above — no ground truth, no independent humans applying the rubric consistently (including unvalidated LLM-as-judge rubrics), OR human evaluation is mentioned but no rubric, rater qualifications, or scoring procedure is disclosed? -> 'None — rubric-only scoring'. This category is the residual bucket — vague human evaluation ('two evaluators judged responses satisfactory') with no rubric or qualifications lands here, not in (2) or (3). RULES: A rubric is NOT a reference standard by itself — what sits BEHIND it decides the type. Do NOT default rubric-scored papers to (4): clinician-applied rubric = (2); trained-coder-applied rubric = (3). Input being a conversation or document does not create a ground truth — judge what the OUTPUT is compared to. Example (Adhikary et al.): ROUGE arm scored against gold summaries = (1); expert Sekhon-framework arm = (2). Result: ['Ground-truth reference', 'Expert/clinician ratings']. Example (LLM judge + expert reference): LLM judge scores generated responses via similarity rubric against expert-authored reference answers from validated textbooks. Type = 'Ground-truth reference' — the reference answers are the target. The LLM judge and similarity rubric are scoring mechanism, not the reference.
reference_standard_type.title: Reference Standard Type

reference_standard_description.description: COMPARATOR, NOT STATISTICS COMPUTED OVER IT (added 2026-08-29.15). Each entry names WHAT AN ARM'S OUTPUTS WERE COMPARED AGAINST. A number computed FROM a comparison is not a comparator: correlations (Pearson, Spearman, Kendall), inter-rater agreement, Cohen's or Fleiss's kappa, Gwet's AC2, accuracy against a majority vote, and averages across raters all belong in scoring_procedures ONLY. NAMED AUTOMATIC METRICS ARE ALSO NOT COMPARATORS (added 2026-08-29.19): AlignScore, BERTScore, ROUGE, BLEU, BARTScore, GPT-Score, perplexity and the like are scoring machinery, not things the outputs were compared against, even though they carry proper names that read like instruments. OBSERVED ERROR: TN-Eval listed 'AlignScore used for faithfulness' as a description entry while also, correctly, recording it in scoring_procedures. Test: does the line name a person, an answer key, an instrument, or a corpus (comparator, record it here), or a statistic (does not belong here)? OBSERVED DUPLICATION: CACTUS carried 'Pearson/Spearman/Kendall correlation of GPT-4o scores with expert scores' in BOTH fields, and MindEval carried 'average psychologist score across annotators'. Lissak is the correct pattern — its kappa and correlations sit in scoring_procedures and are absent here. All reference standards used across the paper's INCLUDED arms, deduplicated. High-level descriptions of the label/score types. E.g. 'Clinician-assigned PHQ-9 scores', 'DSM-5 diagnostic labels', 'Expert consensus ratings', 'Board-exam answer key', 'Gold summaries'. THE TYPE VALUE GOES IN reference_standard_type, NOT HERE (fixed 2026-08-29.15). This field previously instructed 'include exactly None — rubric-only scoring' in the description list, which duplicated a controlled value of reference_standard_type into a free-text field and let a record satisfy the instruction WITHOUT adding the value to the type list. Lissak did exactly that: description item 2 read 'None — rubric-only scoring (for automatic LLM-judge evaluation arms)' while the type list held only Expert/clinician and Trained annotator. Instead, DESCRIBE the arm in plain terms — e.g. 'GPT-4o applying the 5-axis rubric, no human backing for these scores' — and record 'None — rubric-only scoring' in reference_standard_type. COMPARATORS ONLY, NOT STATISTICS COMPUTED OVER THEM (added 2026-08-29.15). Each item names WHAT AN ARM'S OUTPUTS WERE COMPARED AGAINST. Numbers computed FROM a comparison are not comparators: correlations between a judge and human raters, inter-rater kappa or agreement rates, and averages across annotators all belong in scoring_procedures and nowhere else. Two live cases, both duplicated into the wrong field while already correctly present in scoring_procedures: CACTUS's 'Pearson/Spearman/Kendall correlation of GPT-4o scores with expert scores' and MindEval's 'Average psychologist score across annotators'. Lissak is the counter-example done right — its Fleiss's kappa and Spearman correlations appear in scoring_procedures and are correctly absent here. TEST: if the line describes a number derived FROM the standard rather than the standard itself, it is in the wrong field. RUBRIC QUALIFICATION TEST — when a reference standard is a rubric (i.e. 'None — rubric-only scoring' would be entered), the rubric must pass ALL of: (a) Independent-panel test: a second, independent panel of raters given the rubric plus the outputs could produce comparable scores. Rubrics relying on the original raters' shared unstated understanding fail. (b) One-construct-per-item test: each rated construct is its own scored item. A rubric item bundling 'empathy AND clinical accuracy AND coherence' into one 1-5 rating fails — per-construct performance is not recoverable. (c) Higher-vs-lower test: each item explicitly states what distinguishes a higher score from a lower score. Numeric anchors alone (1-5 Likert with endpoints 'poor' and 'excellent') are NOT a rubric. If the rubric fails any of the three, do NOT list it here — enter 'None stated'.SENTINEL: when nothing qualifies, use the exact string 'None stated'. Variants ('Not stated', 'N/A', 'none') are normalised on ingest but should not be produced.
reference_standard_description.title: Reference Standard Description

reference_standard_instruments.description: Named validated clinical or research instruments, AND named study-specific rubrics that derive from a citable published framework, used as reference standards across the paper, deduplicated. Instruments like C-SSRS, PHQ-9, PHQ-8, GAD-7, CAPS-5, HAM-D, MADRS, YMRS, PANSS, WAI, CTRS, MITI, PANAS. PURPOSE: keep instrument names out of benchmark_names — instruments used to score LLM outputs are not benchmarks. This field enables downstream analysis of which validated instruments are used as reference standards across the review, separately from benchmark inputs. WHEN TO POPULATE: only when the LLM's outputs are scored against scores or labels from the instrument, or when raters apply the instrument to evaluate LLM behavior. If the LLM SEES the scale items as input, the scale belongs to benchmark_names, not here. DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA SETS COUNT, BUT DO NOT CLIMB LINEAGE (added 2026-08-29.12). Record DSM-5 (or DSM-IV, ICD-10, ICD-11, RDoC) here when the criteria THEMSELVES are the standard the outputs are judged against — MentalBench derives its per-item diagnostic labels from DSM-5 criteria formalised in a knowledge graph, so DSM-5 belongs here. But record ONLY the standard actually applied. Most named instruments descend from a criteria set — PHQ-9 and PHQ-8 operationalise DSM major depression criteria, GAD-7 the GAD criteria, PCL-5 the PTSD criteria, CAPS-5 likewise — and that ancestry is NEVER recorded. A paper scoring against PHQ-9 gets 'PHQ-9' and NOT 'DSM-5'. A paper scoring against DSM-5 criteria directly gets 'DSM-5'. A paper doing both gets both, one for each arm. TEST: what did the raters or the answer key actually consult? If they applied a scale, record the scale. If they applied the criteria, record the criteria. Never both for the same judgement. This keeps the downstream count of DSM-grounded studies meaningful: without the rule, nearly every depression paper would count as DSM-based by descent, and the column would separate nothing. NAMED RUBRICS GROUNDED IN A PUBLISHED FRAMEWORK ALSO COUNT (widened 2026-08-29.14). Record a study-specific rubric here when the paper states it DERIVES FROM a citable published source — professional-body guidelines, a diagnostic manual, a published scale, or a prior published rubric. Name it as the paper names it with the source in parentheses: 'MindEval rubric (APA clinical supervision guidelines)'. MindEval and Lissak both qualify; both were previously null. THE TEST IS A CITATION, NOT QUALITY. Ask only whether the paper points to a published source the rubric came from. Do not judge how good, how detailed, or how well-anchored the rubric is, and do not credit a rubric merely because clinicians helped write it — expert authorship without a cited source is still an author-authored rubric. DO NOT CLIMB LINEAGE, exactly as for DSM above. Record the source the rubric actually cites, not that source's ancestry. WHY THIS FIELD IS WIDER THAN IT LOOKS. Populating it does NOT make the rubric a reference standard. reference_standard_type asks whether anything external adjudicated these particular scores; this field asks what measuring device was used and whether it is a recognised one. A validated instrument applied by an LLM judge with no human backing is still 'None — rubric-only scoring' in the type field — CACTUS is exactly that. Crossing the two fields is what distinguishes an expert-designed rubric-only evaluation (MindEval, Lissak) from an ad hoc one (Hasan, WundtGPT), which is otherwise invisible. THE INSTRUMENT MUST BE USED AS THE REFERENCE STANDARD (added 2026-08-29.19). This field records instruments the OUTPUTS WERE JUDGED AGAINST, not every named instrument the paper touches. An instrument used to BUILD the stimuli — to write prompts, select or stratify cases, define severity tiers for sampling, or ground a scenario — is apparatus and does NOT belong here; note it in abstraction_notes instead. TEST: were model outputs scored against this instrument? If it never touches the scoring, leave it out. OBSERVED ERROR: a chatbot risk-escalation study recorded PHQ-9 here while its reference standard was an author-defined protocol (rubric-only) and its scoring procedures counted referral and shutdown prompt numbers — PHQ-9 shaped the escalating prompts and scored nothing. Stable across three runs, so a consistent misreading rather than noise. LEAVE None when the reference standard is exact match to gold responses, or an author-authored rubric with NO cited published source. Hasan's five counselling dimensions and WundtGPT's four dimensions are invented for those papers and stay null — that is the contrast the cross-tab depends on.CONVENTION: use null (not an empty list) when this field does not apply to the paper. An empty list is never a valid value for this field.
reference_standard_instruments.title: Reference Standard Instruments

scoring_procedures.description: All scoring procedures used across the paper's INCLUDED arms, deduplicated. High-level descriptions of the measurement operation and its OUTPUT (metric, scale, count, or structured category). INCLUDED ARMS ONLY: exclude scoring procedures belonging solely to arms that failed the MH relevance gate. If a procedure is used in both an included and an excluded arm, it stays (via its use in the included arm). E.g. 'accuracy and macro-F1 against reference labels', '5-point Likert per dimension, averaged across 3 raters', 'binary safety flag per response, percentage flagged reported', 'ROUGE-L against reference answer'. Include exactly 'None stated' if an included arm uses no scoring procedure. WORKED EXAMPLE: a paper has 3 arms — Arm 1 evaluates BERT vs GPT-4 on a generic sentiment task (excluded, not MH); Arm 2 evaluates GPT-4 on PsyQA with ROUGE-L against reference answers (MH-relevant); Arm 3 evaluates GPT-4 on a depression severity task with accuracy against clinician-labeled severity tiers (MH-relevant). scoring_procedures lists only ['ROUGE-L against reference answers', 'Accuracy against clinician-labeled severity tiers']. Arm 1's scoring does not appear.SENTINEL: when nothing qualifies, use the exact string 'None stated'. Variants ('Not stated', 'N/A', 'none') are normalised on ingest but should not be produced.
scoring_procedures.title: Scoring Procedures

abstraction_flags.description: Free-form list of field names where interpretation was genuinely uncertain — a different reader could reasonably code the field differently, or something about the paper was confusing to the abstractor. NOT for missing information (use the field's own value for that). Common candidates: system_tasks, evaluation_constructs_categories, reference_standard_type, reference_standard_description, type_of_study, benchmark_names. Null if no genuine ambiguity.CONVENTION: use null (not an empty list) when this field does not apply to the paper. An empty list is never a valid value for this field.
abstraction_flags.title: Abstraction Flags

abstraction_notes.description: Free-form prose notes accompanying abstraction_flags. Required if abstraction_flags is non-null; for each flagged field, name the alternative interpretation and briefly explain what made the call unclear. Null if abstraction_flags is null.
abstraction_notes.title: Abstraction Notes

benchmark.description: The benchmark this row describes. Copied EXACTLY from the BENCHMARK LIST in the user message. '[unnamed]' only when the list says so.
benchmark.title: Benchmark

scored.description: True if the paper reports an MH-disaggregated result of a generative LLM on THIS benchmark. False if the benchmark is only mentioned, used for training, or listed without results.
scored.title: Scored

scored_notes.description: Required when scored=false: one sentence saying why (training-only, listed without results, no MH-disaggregated result). Null when scored=true.
scored_notes.title: Scored Notes

models_tested.description: Generative LLMs scored on THIS benchmark. [] when scored=false. See BENCHMARK-LEVEL FIELDS.
models_tested.title: Models Tested

input_modality.description: Modalities of this benchmark's items, lowercase: text / audio / video / image / multimodal (text+audio) / multimodal (text+video) / multimodal (text+image) / other.
input_modality.title: Input Modality

n_test_cases.description: Distinct items on this benchmark the model is scored on. Null if not reported or scored=false.
n_test_cases.title: N Test Cases

n_test_cases_notes.description: Qualifier if ambiguous (test split, sample of a larger set). Null if unambiguous.
n_test_cases_notes.title: N Test Cases Notes

input_source_grounding.description: Category + who authored/validated the items + whether independent. No content/format description.
input_source_grounding.title: Input Source Grounding

input_lived_experience_role.description: None / Consulted / Co-design / Led — lived-experience involvement in item design or validation.
input_lived_experience_role.title: Input Lived Experience Role

prompt_variation_testing.description: Prompt-robustness testing on this benchmark and its effect, or 'Not reported'.
prompt_variation_testing.title: Prompt Variation Testing

evaluation_engine.description: '<prefix> (specifier)' with prefix one of: LLM as judge / Automated metric / Human raters / Multi-judge (hybrid; ...) / Statistical comparison / Other.
evaluation_engine.title: Evaluation Engine

rubric_source_grounding.description: Where the scoring criteria came from and validation status, or EXACTLY 'Not applicable — automated metric'.
rubric_source_grounding.title: Rubric Source Grounding

scoring_lived_experience_role.description: None / Consulted / Co-design / Led — lived-experience involvement in scoring design or validation.
scoring_lived_experience_role.title: Scoring Lived Experience Role

judge_validation_reliability.description: Judge reliability evidence, 'Not reported', 'Not applicable — automated metric', or 'Not reported — single rater, IRR not possible'.
judge_validation_reliability.title: Judge Validation Reliability

scoring_reproducibility_notes.description: Always required — what scoring materials are available, what is missing, why the rating.
scoring_reproducibility_notes.title: Scoring Reproducibility Notes

name.description: Model name as given in the paper. Generative LLMs only — omit logistic regression, SVMs, fine-tuned encoders (BERT-family), rule-based systems, and any judge / simulator model.
name.title: Name

role.description: 'Baseline/comparator' only if this generative LLM is a comparison point rather than a primary evaluation focus. Null if it is a primary subject of evaluation.
role.title: Role

arms.description: Exactly one arm per benchmark in the BENCHMARK LIST, in the same order.
arms.title: Arms
